legend: Define a number b%%ZSMJ0%% to be a subsequence of a number a%%ZSMJ1%% if, when you write out a%%ZSMJ2%% in decimal notation, you can erase some (but not all) of its digits so that the remaining digits, in order, form b%%ZSMJ3%%. For example, 356%%ZSMJ4%% is a subsequence of 1234567%%ZSMJ5%%, because you can erase the 1%%ZSMJ6%%, 2%%ZSMJ7%%, 4%%ZSMJ8%%, and 7%%ZSMJ9%% to form 356%%ZSMJ10%%. However, 0%%ZSMJ11%% is not a subsequence of 23527%%ZSMJ12%%, because the digit 0%%ZSMJ13%% is not present in 23527%%ZSMJ14%%.

You are given a number x%%ZSMJ15%%. Find any number n%%ZSMJ16%% such that the MEX%%ZSMJ17%% of the set of all subsequences of n%%ZSMJ18%% is equal to x%%ZSMJ19%%. It can be shown that such an n%%ZSMJ20%% always exists.

The MEX%%ZSMJ21%% of a set of integers is defined as the smallest non-negative integer which does not occur in the set. For example, the MEX%%ZSMJ22%% of {0,1,2,4}%%ZSMJ23%% is 3%%ZSMJ24%%, and the MEX%%ZSMJ25%% of {1,4,6,8}%%ZSMJ26%% is 0%%ZSMJ27%%.
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ28%% (1≤t≤1000%%ZSMJ29%%) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows.

Each test case consists of a single line containing an integer x%%ZSMJ30%% (1≤x<1010000%%ZSMJ31%%) — the desired MEX%%ZSMJ32%% of the subsequences of n%%ZSMJ33%%. It is guaranteed that x%%ZSMJ34%% does not contain any leading zeroes.
It is guaranteed that the sum of the number of digits of x%%ZSMJ35%% across all test cases is at most 10000%%ZSMJ36%%.
output: For each test case, output a single positive integer n%%ZSMJ37%% — any number such that the MEX%%ZSMJ38%% of its subsequences is x%%ZSMJ39%%. n%%ZSMJ40%% may not contain leading zeroes.
If there are multiple solutions, you may print any.
The sum of the number of digits of n%%ZSMJ41%% across all test cases must not exceed 106%%ZSMJ42%%.
note: In the first sample case, the subsequences of 70%%ZSMJ43%% are 7%%ZSMJ44%%, 0%%ZSMJ45%%, and 70%%ZSMJ46%%, and the MEX%%ZSMJ47%% of {0,7,70}%%ZSMJ48%% is 1%%ZSMJ49%%.
In the second sample case, 12836880457%%ZSMJ50%% contains every digit except 9%%ZSMJ51%%, and therefore the MEX%%ZSMJ52%% of its subsequences is 9%%ZSMJ53%%.
